title: The Company as an Operating System
summary: An operating system manages hardware for programs; a company OS manages people, money, and attention for projects.
body:
Company OS: the operating system of a business — how work is scheduled, how resources are allocated, how permissions flow, and how the whole thing stays running. Real OS concepts, applied to companies.

An operating system manages hardware for programs; a company OS manages people, money, and attention for projects. Both need scheduling (who works on what), memory management (budgets), permissions (who decides), and inter-process communication (meetings, docs). The metaphor is structural, not decorative.

title: Scheduling: Who Works on What
summary: OS schedulers allocate CPU fairly; companies allocate people.
body:
OS schedulers allocate CPU fairly; companies allocate people. Round-robin (rotate the on-call), priority scheduling (the big client first), and real-time scheduling (production incidents preempt everything) all have company analogs.

# Round-robin scheduler: the OS concept behind fair task sharing
from collections import deque
def round_robin(tasks, quantum=2):
    q = deque((name, burst) for name, burst in tasks)
    t = 0
    while q:
        name, burst = q.popleft()
        run = min(quantum, burst)
        t += run; burst -= run
        print(f"t={t:3d}  {name} ran {run} (remaining {burst})")
        if burst: q.append((name, burst))
round_robin([("email",5),("report",3),("calls",4)])

title: Permissions and Access Control

title: Memory Management: Budgets
summary: RAM is finite; so is cash.

RAM is finite; so is cash. Paging (swap projects in/out of focus), memory leaks (zombie projects consuming budget), and garbage collection (killing dead initiatives) are budget disciplines with OS names.

title: The Kernel: Leadership's Real Job
summary: The kernel doesn't do the work — it enables it: scheduling, protection, abstraction.
body:
The kernel doesn't do the work — it enables it: scheduling, protection, abstraction. Leaders who micromanage are kernels running user code: slow, fragile, wrong layer. Good kernels set policy; processes do the work.
